content.title: About
content.content: Pea salad is a dish made from boiled or canned green peas, often combined with vegetables, herbs, mayonnaise or a light yogurt‑based dressing. It has a mildly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture, suitable as a side dish or a light main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas are one of the oldest legume crops, cultivated for over 7,000 years.
There are more than 30 varieties of peas, including sweet, garden, and snap peas.
Peas are a good source of plant protein and are widely used in vegetarian diets.
In many traditional cuisines (e.g., Russian, Polish, Indian) pea salad is a classic comfort food.
Dried peas can be stored for several years when kept in a cool, dry place.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain vitamin B6, folate, and thiamine, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They supply iron, magnesium, phosphorus and zinc, supporting blood and bone health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Peas raise blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for weight control and diabetes management.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause increased gas in sensitive people.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid may reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting can mitigate this.

items.title: Sodium in prepared salad
items.content: If the salad is dressed with mayonnaise or soy sauce, sodium levels can be high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pea salad chilled as an appetizer, a side to meat or fish, or as a light meal. Enhance it with boiled eggs, ham, fresh vegetables, herbs, and a simple dressing of yogurt, lemon juice and olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. If storing without dressing, keep the peas and vegetables separate to preserve freshness.
